question: Which bloodborne pathogen is most efficiently transmitted through contaminated medical injections?
explanation: Parenteral exposure via contaminated needles carries a very high transmission efficiency for bloodborne viruses, particularly hepatitis C, hepatitis B, and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary operational hazard of reusing a disposable plastic syringe in clinical practice?

options.C: Microscopic dulling of the needle bevel
options.D: Rapid degradation of the plastic barrel

explanation: Pathogens left inside the dead space of a syringe or needle can directly enter the bloodstream of the next patient, causing systemic infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what defines a safe injection?

options.A: An injection that utilizes a retractable needle and a safety-engineered winged set
options.B: One that causes no harm to the recipient, poses no risk to the provider, and creates no hazardous waste
options.C: Any parenteral medication delivery performed inside a sterile operating theater
options.D: One that is administered exclusively by a registered physician using a glass syringe

explanation: The WHO comprehensive definition explicitly encompasses the safety of the patient, the healthcare worker, and the surrounding community. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the first operational step a nurse should take to align with WHO core injection safety principles?

options.A: Soak all used metal needles in a strong chlorine solution before disposal
options.B: Assess whether an oral alternative to the prescribed medication is clinically effective
options.C: Recap every syringe immediately after administration to protect colleagues
options.D: Store used safety boxes in the patient ward until the end of the shift

explanation: Reducing unnecessary injections by selecting oral routes whenever possible is a core preventative tenet of global injection safety guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is recognized as the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections during clinical procedures?

options.C: Wearing heavy utility gloves at all times

explanation: Hand hygiene interrupts the transmission of pathogens carried on the hands of healthcare workers between patients and sterile equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: When must a nurse perform hand hygiene in relation to preparing an aseptic injection?

options.A: Only when the patient has a known infectious disease diagnosis
options.B: Before entering the hospital ward at the start of the morning shift
options.C: After disposing of the used syringe into the safety box
options.D: Immediately before preparing the medication and after the procedure is finished

explanation: Aseptic technique requires hand hygiene immediately prior to touching sterile supplies to avoid introducing environmental microbes into the medication pathway. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanical feature of an Auto-Disable (AD) syringe?

options.A: It automatically jams or breaks after a single injection to prevent reuse
options.B: It measures exact dosages without requiring manual plunger alignment
options.C: It neutralizes bloodborne viruses using an internal chemical coating
options.D: It features a built-in metal shield that covers the needle tip upon impact

explanation: Auto-disable technology is engineered to render the syringe permanently inoperable after one complete stroke, eliminating accidental or intentional reuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is pre-filling multiple syringes prior to a mass immunization clinic strongly discouraged?

options.A: It compromises sterility and creates high risks of bacterial growth and medication errors
options.B: It causes the plastic barrel to dissolve when exposed to ambient room lighting
options.C: It increases the total weight of the medication tray beyond safe carrying limits
options.D: It forces the plunger mechanism to lock before the nurse reaches the patient

explanation: Drawn medications left sitting in syringes lose sterility and run a high risk of microbial proliferation or being administered to the wrong recipient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended fill level for a sharps disposal container before it must be permanently sealed?
explanation: Stopping at the three-quarters mark prevents accidental punctures that occur when pushing items into an overly packed container. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT permitted when handling used injection equipment?

options.A: Discarding the syringe and needle as a single unit without separation
options.B: Recapping the needle with two hands immediately after an injection
options.C: Inspecting the container to ensure it rests on a stable surface
options.D: Placing the puncture-resistant safety box close to the point of use

explanation: Manual recapping is a primary cause of needle-stick injuries and is strictly prohibited by international safety standards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Apply a concentrated iodine tincture and cover with airtight tape
options.B: Soak the affected finger in a basin of domestic bleach solution
options.C: Squeeze the wound vigorously to force out all trapped venous blood
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and clean running water

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water removes surface contaminants, while harsh scrubbing or caustic chemicals should be avoided to prevent mucosal damage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: When does the highest risk of sustaining a needle-stick injury typically occur during a clinical procedure?

options.A: While opening the sterile paper packaging of a brand-new syringe
options.B: While administering oral medications to an uncooperative patient
options.C: When sliding an unpunctured safety box into a transport carton
options.D: During or immediately after attempting to recap a used needle

explanation: Attempts to guide a contaminated needle back into its small cap frequently result in missed entries and finger punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is a primary logistical barrier to maintaining injection safety in resource-limited clinical settings?

options.A: Interrupted supply chains for auto-disable syringes and safety boxes
options.B: Lack of patient willingness to receive any form of intramuscular therapy
options.C: Excessive availability of sterile glass syringes and autoclaves
options.D: Overabundance of professional nursing personnel in rural clinics

explanation: Stockouts of safety-engineered devices and disposal containers often force clinicians into improvised, hazardous practices. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h7)

question: How can a nurse leader effectively monitor and improve injection safety compliance on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Require patients to purchase and bring their own disposable needles
options.B: Conduct supportive supervision and ensure continuous availability of safety boxes
options.C: Punish junior staff publicly whenever an injection error is reported
options.D: Prohibit the administration of all parenteral medications across the facility

explanation: Supportive supervision combined with reliable supplies creates an enabling environment where safety protocols can be consistently followed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h7)
